Modular Brush Lab

A working model of the next Brush Lab in Inkwash. A brush has six parts, top to bottom: Tip, Medium, Smudge, Paper, Drying and Control. Tap a part to see each of its choices drawn with your brush, and try the brush in the test area.

Checks






  
How it works

  
    
    
  1. Parts. Always in the same order: Tip, Medium, Smudge, Paper, Drying, Control. Each part has one choice. Off and None count as choices, so every combination draws something.
    2. 
    
  2. Swap. Tap a part and the strip under the test area shows your brush with each of that part's choices. Tap one to use it. Undo puts it back.
    3. 
    
  3. Simple. One slider per part, labelled by what it does, plus the styles, Randomize, a few words about the brush, the six slots and the library.
    4. 
    
  4. Advanced. Lock a part and roll the rest. Tap a part to open all its dials; each has its own lock and dice. Underneath are six variations, and one of them may swap a whole part.
    5. 
    
  5. Drying. Quick, the default, keeps the last few millimetres behind the nib wet while you draw, and nothing moves after you lift. Instant dries under the nib. Slow keeps changing until it's dry. Float lets ink sit on water until you print it.
    6. 
    
  6. Float. Suminagashi: the paint floats on water. A tap drops a ring and a drag lays a film. It prints onto the paper when its floating time runs out, or when you tap Print.
    7. 
    
  7. Codes. Load shows this brush's share code, ready to copy, and a box to paste one in. The app's older I and P codes and the prototypes' codes still load and draw as before.
    8.
